title: Don't flag retired or done items that depend on a retired item
lead: `check` rejects an edge onto a retired item even when the item holding the edge is itself retired or done. Neither kind of item will ever be started, so the edge is history, not drift.
findings_note: user report: check flags retired items that depend on retired items; user cleared the edges to pass
boundary: **Not in this slice:** restoring edges users already cleared to get past this; any change to `remove`'s dependents guard; re-validating edges when an item is un-retired.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Reported from real use. A user retired S28/S29/S34/S49/S50 while some of them depended on each other, and `check` failed. To get past it they had to delete those dependency edges, which throws away the record of how the retired work fit together.

A done item has the same problem. Its work already landed, so retiring one of its prerequisites afterwards (say, a spike that turned out to be the wrong path) should not break `check`. The error text, "this item can never be started", is false for a done item.

The rule is in two places, and neither looks at the dependent's own status:

- `verify.py:116-128` adds an error for every `item.depends_on` entry that names a retired item.
- `ops.py:119` (`_validate_depends`) refuses any proposed dependency list that names a retired item. It checks the whole list, not just edges the change adds, so editing any edge of a retired or done item that still points at a retired item is refused too. The docstring says "Edges the change does not touch are left alone"; this branch doesn't follow that.

The rule exists to catch live work that is blocked forever. A retired or done dependent is not live work.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. When A depends on B and both are retired, `verify` and `check` exit 0 with no finding for A.
2. When A is done and depends on retired B, `verify` and `check` exit 0 with no finding for A.
3. When A is open, started or parked and depends on retired B, `verify`/`check` still fail with the existing message. `test_Verify_DependsOnRetiredItem_IsReported` and `test_Check_DependsOnRetired_Fails` keep passing unchanged.
4. Retiring A (with `--force`) after it already depends on retired B leaves `check` clean.
5. `set A --depends-on B` succeeds when B is retired and A is retired or done.
6. An open item still cannot gain a new edge onto a retired item; `test_Set_RetiredDependency_IsRefused` keeps passing.
7. Un-retiring A (`set A --status open`) while it still depends on retired B makes `check` report A again, because A is now live and blocked.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
In both places, skip the retired-dependency finding or refusal when the dependent's own status is `cfg.retired_status` or `cfg.done_status`. Leave the dangling-id and cycle checks as they are for retired and done items: an unknown id or a cycle is still a data error.

`set --status` does not re-validate edges, so un-retiring A goes through, and `check` catches it (test 7). This slice adds no refusal there.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check` and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap. Add a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased (fix).
